decision_conditions: The proposed extension by reason of its excessive height, depth, footprint, bulk and massing would fail to be in keeping with the established pattern of ground floor rear extensions within the locality, detracting from the overall character of the area. The proposal would therefore be contrary to Policies D3 of the London Plan (2021), CP30 of the Core Strategy (2010), DMD11 and DMD37 of the Development Management Document (2014) as well as the aims and intentions outlined within the NPPF (2024).

The proposed extension by virtue of its siting, excessive height and rearward projection in respect to neighbouring properties at No. 60 and 56 The Mall, would appear as an unneighbourly and overbearing form of development that would unduly restrict light, outlook and visual amenity afforded to the rear gardens and adjacent habitable room windows of these neighbouring properties, and in the case of No. 60 the development would create an unacceptable sense of enclosure in respect to this neighbour's garden and adjacent rear facing habitable room windows. Furthermore, the proposed rear patio, by reason of its height and siting, would enable harmful overlooking of the rear gardens and adjacent rear facing habitable room windows of both No. 60 and 56 The Mall. The proposal would therefore be contrary to Policies D6 of the London Plan (2021), CP30 of the Core Strategy (2010), policy DMD8 of the Development Management Document (2014) as well as the aims and intentions outlined within the NPPF (2024).
description: Single storey rear extension, with associated rear patio
